gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Garmin's 'unlimited with solar' battery for the Instinct 3 Solar, its top pick, holds only with all-day wear and 3 hours a day outdoors at 50,000 lux, about 150,000 lux-hours a day. Without that, the 45 mm is a 28-day watch and the 50 mm a 40-day watch in smartwatch mode.
standout_why: I compared against mobileplustech.com, the cited page. It says only that solar 'adds hours or days per week in sunny conditions, according to makers', with no lux or hour figures. smartwatchestrends.com says 'unlimited battery in certain use conditions with enough sunlight' and only for the Instinct 2X. The cited TechRadar T-Rex 3 Pro review and techradar.com/best/garmin-watch came back with headline only, so I couldn't check what they say about solar. None of the pages I could read gives the condition, the battery life without solar, or a measured solar gain.
decides: This confirms the Instinct 3 Solar for men who work or hike outdoors with the watch face uncovered. DC Rainmaker measured about 20 points of charge from 3 h 45 min of winter sun. It weakens the Solar pick for an office worker, or anyone whose sleeve covers the watch. For them it is a 28-day (45 mm) or 40-day (50 mm) watch, close to the 27 days ChatGPT quoted for the Amazfit T-Rex 3, so solar is no longer the reason to choose it. Garmin itself says solar is 'not intended as the primary charging source'.

findings.label: Smartwatch-mode battery, without and with solar
findings.value: Up to 28 days typical use; 'Unlimited with solar' (footnote 1)
findings.source_title: Instinct 3 Solar Series Owner's Manual - Battery Life Information
findings.note: Garmin's US manual. Footnote 1 reads: 'Assuming all-day wear with 3 hours per day outside in 50,000 lux conditions'.

findings.label: Smartwatch-mode battery, without and with solar
findings.value: Up to 40 days typical use; 'Unlimited with solar' (footnote 1)
findings.source_title: Instinct 3 Solar Series Owner's Manual - Battery Life Information
findings.note: Same table. 3 h × 50,000 lux = 150,000 lux-hours a day needed for 'unlimited'. Without solar the average drain is 100/40 ≈ 2.5 % a day for the 50 mm and 100/28 ≈ 3.6 % a day for the 45 mm.

findings.label: GPS battery, without and with solar (all-systems multi-band)
findings.value: 45 mm: 24 h → 40 h with solar; 50 mm: 34 h → 60 h with solar. Only Max Battery GPS mode is 'unlimited with solar'.
findings.source_title: Instinct 3 Solar Series Owner's Manual - Battery Life Information
findings.note: GPS footnotes assume 'use outside in 50,000 lux conditions' (plus SatIQ for multi-band). GPS-only mode: 40 h → 130 h (45 mm) and 60 h → 260 h (50 mm).

findings.label: Garmin's stated role of solar and wearing advice
findings.value: 'While not intended as the primary charging source…'; 'Weather conditions and sun positioning may impact charging efficiency'; advises to 'avoid covering it with clothing'
findings.source_title: Why you should use Garmin smartwatches with solar charging (Garmin blog, 2025-03-24)
findings.note: The page repeats the Instinct 3 Solar footnote: 'Assumes all-day wear with 3 hours per day outside in 50,000 lux conditions.'

findings.label: Measured solar gain (DC Rainmaker)
findings.value: 20 % → 40 % in about 3 h 45 min, mostly sunny winter day, 328k lux-hours (second 50 mm unit 20 % → 38 % at 287k lux-hours)
findings.source_title: DC Rainmaker, Garmin Instinct 3 In-Depth Review: AMOLED & Solar (2025-01-30)
findings.note: DC Rainmaker calls 50,000 lux 'a slightly (thin/light clouds) hazy sun, even in the winter'. My scaling: 20 points / 328k lux-hours ≈ 0.061 points per 1k lux-hours, so Garmin's 150k lux-hours ≈ 9 points a day against about 2.5 % daily drain. That is linear scaling from one winter test, not a Garmin figure. He couldn't explain why the two identical 50 mm units gained different amounts. In a second test (about 5 h 30 min, sunny then cloudy) the units went 36 % → 51 % at 517k lux-hours.

findings.label: Solar on the AMOLED version
findings.value: None ('the AMOLED edition doesn't have any solar functionality')
findings.source_title: DC Rainmaker, Garmin Instinct 3 In-Depth Review: AMOLED & Solar (2025-01-30)
findings.note: On a 12-hour mountain hike (GPS-only, navigation on) DC Rainmaker estimated 75 h for the Solar against 41 h for the AMOLED.

findings.label: Solar-intensity readout on launch firmware
findings.value: Sun icon and solar gains not shown on production firmware at review; beta firmware 7.xx or later needed
findings.source_title: DC Rainmaker, Garmin Instinct 3 In-Depth Review: AMOLED & Solar (2025-01-30)
findings.note: Matters only to a buyer checking whether they reach 50,000 lux. Current firmware probably fixes this, but I didn't check.
